node.label: Legislative Councils
node.summary: State upper Houses (Art. 168-172): who has them, how they're formed and abolished, their powers.

facts.text: Parliament's **PAC** has **22 members** (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha) and since **1967** has been chaired by an **Opposition** member; it examines **CAG** reports. The CAG is appointed under **Article 148**.
facts.plain: Parliament's PAC has 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha) and since 1967 has been chaired by an Opposition member; it examines CAG reports. The CAG is appointed under Article 148.

facts.text: LS Speaker **Om Birla** opened a conference of **Public Accounts Committee** chairs of 25 States at the Keralam Assembly; he flagged PAC reports pending for 15-20 years and backed AI for audit analysis. Parliament's PAC chair: **K.C. Venugopal** (Congress).
facts.plain: LS Speaker Om Birla opened a conference of Public Accounts Committee chairs of 25 States at the Keralam Assembly; he flagged PAC reports pending for 15-20 years and backed AI for audit analysis. Parliament's PAC chair: K.C. Venugopal (Congress).

facts.text: Debate: supporters see a check on hasty laws and a voice for graduates and teachers; critics see a costly House for defeated leaders. The article says reform them or abolish them.
facts.plain: Debate: supporters see a check on hasty laws and a voice for graduates and teachers; critics see a costly House for defeated leaders. The article says reform them or abolish them.

facts.text: **Second ARC (2007)** suggested turning Councils into 'councils of local governments' elected only by local body members, to strengthen local self-government.
facts.plain: Second ARC (2007) suggested turning Councils into 'councils of local governments' elected only by local body members, to strengthen local self-government.

facts.text: Tamil Nadu's Council was abolished in **1986** (MGR as CM); a 2010 revival resolution was reversed in 2011. Andhra Pradesh's was abolished in **1985** (NTR) and re-created in **2007**.
facts.plain: Tamil Nadu's Council was abolished in 1986 (MGR as CM); a 2010 revival resolution was reversed in 2011. Andhra Pradesh's was abolished in 1985 (NTR) and re-created in 2007.

facts.text: The **Government of India Act, 1935** created bicameral legislatures in six provinces: Madras, Bombay, Bengal, United Provinces, Bihar, Assam. Members then served 9 years.
facts.plain: The Government of India Act, 1935 created bicameral legislatures in six provinces: Madras, Bombay, Bengal, United Provinces, Bihar, Assam. Members then served 9 years.

facts.text: Delay power comes from **Art. 197** (3 months, then 1 month on re-passage). On Money Bills the Council can only recommend (**Art. 198**, 14 days).
facts.plain: Delay power comes from Art. 197 (3 months, then 1 month on re-passage). On Money Bills the Council can only recommend (Art. 198, 14 days).

facts.text: Weak powers: no joint sitting, the Assembly's version prevails, and the Council can delay a bill by at most **four months**.
facts.plain: Weak powers: no joint sitting, the Assembly's version prevails, and the Council can delay a bill by at most four months.

facts.text: **Art. 172**: a permanent House, never dissolved. Members serve **6 years**; one-third retire every **2 years**. Ministers, including the CM, can be Council members.
facts.plain: Art. 172: a permanent House, never dissolved. Members serve 6 years; one-third retire every 2 years. Ministers, including the CM, can be Council members.

facts.text: **Art. 171**: Council strength at most **one-third** of the Assembly and at least **40**. Members: 1/3 elected by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/6 nominated by the Governor.
facts.plain: Art. 171: Council strength at most one-third of the Assembly and at least 40. Members: 1/3 elected by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/6 nominated by the Governor.

facts.text: **Art. 169**: Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law, after the State Assembly passes a resolution by a **two-thirds majority**.
facts.plain: Art. 169: Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law, after the State Assembly passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority.

facts.text: Six States have a Legislative Council: **Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka** (Art. 168). 28 Council seats were contested last week in UP, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
facts.plain: Six States have a Legislative Council: Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka (Art. 168). 28 Council seats were contested last week in UP, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
keys: Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka

facts.text: MLC voter rules: a graduate voter needs a degree held for at least **3 years**; a teacher voter must have taught **3 years** in a secondary school or higher. They must register on a separate roll.
facts.plain: MLC voter rules: a graduate voter needs a degree held for at least 3 years; a teacher voter must have taught 3 years in a secondary school or higher. They must register on a separate roll.

facts.text: Recent MLC polls covered **28 seats**: U.P. 11, Bihar 8, Maharashtra 5, Karnataka 4; the **BJP won 13**. In Karnataka the **BJP-JD(S)** swept all four. Voting is by **proportional representation (single transferable vote)**.
facts.plain: Recent MLC polls covered 28 seats: U.P. 11, Bihar 8, Maharashtra 5, Karnataka 4; the BJP won 13. In Karnataka the BJP-JD(S) swept all four. Voting is by proportional representation (single transferable vote).

facts.text: Coalitions in Maharashtra: **Mahayuti** = BJP + Shiv Sena + NCP; **Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA)** = Congress + Shiv Sena (UBT) + NCP (SP). State Congress chief: **Harshwardhan Sapkal**.
facts.plain: Coalitions in Maharashtra: Mahayuti = BJP + Shiv Sena + NCP; Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) = Congress + Shiv Sena (UBT) + NCP (SP). State Congress chief: Harshwardhan Sapkal.

facts.text: Maharashtra MLC polls (5 seats, voting 23 Oct): Opposition **MVA 3**, ruling **Mahayuti 2**. Congress's **Abhijeet Wanjari** retained **Nagpur Graduates'**, beating BJP's Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes; the BJP had held that seat for 58 years before 2020. NCP(SP) won Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Graduates'.
facts.plain: Maharashtra MLC polls (5 seats, voting 23 Oct): Opposition MVA 3, ruling Mahayuti 2. Congress's Abhijeet Wanjari retained Nagpur Graduates', beating BJP's Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes; the BJP had held that seat for 58 years before 2020. NCP(SP) won Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Graduates'.

facts.text: U.P. MLC polls (11 Graduates' and Teachers' seats, held on **ballot papers**): **BJP 6, SP 5**, including both Varanasi seats; SP won only 3 in 2020. In Gorakhpur-Faizabad the BJP margin was just **307 votes**.
